text: The fields specify a finitely generated full ℤ-submodule, a symmetric ℚ-bilinear form, and integer values on its carrier. Fullness identifies the ambient space with its rationalization, matching [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Degenerate forms remain allowed; affine A₁ supplies the published degeneracy control. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L336) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L138) passes.
The explicit Gram lattice with matrix [[2,-2],[-2,2]] is a valid object with degenerate form.
The Gram construction has the actual integer coordinate carrier, not the whole rational ambient space.

Applying L to x,y evaluates its ambient rational form L.form x y, exactly the extension of the pairing in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The arguments range over V; integer-valuedness is required only on carrier vectors. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L89) passes.
The coercion evaluates to L.form on every pair of ambient vectors.

The type denoted by L is the subtype of vectors in L.carrier, so its elements carry lattice membership. This realizes the underlying integer module of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), while V remains the rational ambient space. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L122) passes.
The rank-one example has carrier precisely the embedded integers.

This Prop class asserts precisely nondegeneracy of the ambient rational bilinear form. Fullness makes this equivalent to having no nonzero lattice vector orthogonal to the entire lattice. The separate predicate agrees with [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), which also permits degenerate lattices. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L336) passes.
The affine Gram example exists without the nondegeneracy mixin.

The instance exposes the stored L.isLattice certificate: finite generation and full rational span. These are exactly the two conditions in [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67); symmetry and integrality are additional lattice-structure fields. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L115) passes.
The resulting carrier basis extends to the same ambient vectors.

A finite ℤ-basis of the carrier extends to a ℚ-basis of V, so V is finite-dimensional. Finite generation and torsion-freeness over ℤ provide the finite free carrier; [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67) supplies the extension. No nondegeneracy is needed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L124) passes.
The finite integral and rational dimensions agree, including rank zero.

The carrier inclusion into its dual followed by [Mathlib’s integral dual pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40) gives the ℤ-bilinear restriction. Its integer value is uniquely determined by its cast to ℚ equalling L.form x y, so the construction is canonical and contains no factor of two. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L159) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L175) passes.
Casting the restricted integer value recovers the original rational pairing.
The restricted pairing retains symmetry.

Carrier and rational form are the only data fields; fullness, symmetry and integrality are propositions. Their proof irrelevance therefore makes these two equalities sufficient for literal equality of lattices. The data match [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); this is equality in a fixed ambient space. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L191) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L196) passes.
The constructor preserves the specified carrier.
The constructor preserves the specified rational form.

The conclusion is exactly the nondegenerate-form field of the IsNondegenerate assumption. It exposes the predicate used in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) without adding definiteness or unimodularity hypotheses. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L336) passes.
A degenerate example verifies that nondegeneracy is not built into every object.

L.le_dual applied to the membership proofs of x and y gives L.form x y∈(1:Submodule ℤ ℚ). By [Mathlib’s integral dual pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40), this submodule is the image of ℤ, so the statement is exactly integer-valuedness on lattice vectors. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L159) passes.
The integer witness is realized by the restricted integral form.

The dual pairing selects an integer whose image is the rational value; inclusion into the dual leaves x unchanged. Thus the cast of the integral restriction is exactly L.form x y, by [Mathlib’s integral dual pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40), with no scaling or sign change. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L301) passes.
On a Gram basis the integer pairing recovers Gij exactly.

After casting both sides to ℚ, symmetry becomes L.form x y=L.form y x. Injectivity of ℤ→ℚ then gives integer symmetry. This verifies the symmetric restricted pairing of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) without any nondegeneracy premise. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L159) passes.
Both sides of the integer symmetry assertion cast to the symmetric ambient pairing.

If N⊆L.carrier, every pair of N-vectors is a pair of lattice vectors and hence has integral pairing. By [Mathlib’s integral dual pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40), this is precisely N⊆Nᵛ. The theorem asserts integrality and does not assert that N has full rational span. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L97) passes.
The containing carrier supplies integer values for all pairs of its vectors.

The carrier is the ℤ-span of b and the form is xᵀGy in b-coordinates. Integral symmetric G gives integral symmetric pairing on that span, exactly the Gram construction in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) and [Mathlib’s matrix–bilinear-form equivalence](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L191). Singular matrices are permitted. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L103) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L336) passes.
The hyperbolic Gram construction recovers [[0,1],[1,0]] in the integral basis.
The singular affine Cartan matrix constructs a valid degenerate lattice.

The constructor packages S and B with the supplied fullness, symmetry and integrality proofs. Its IsLattice hypothesis means both finite generation and full rational span, as in [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67); an arbitrary submodule is not silently treated as full. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L191) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L196) passes.
The underlying integer submodule is exactly S.
The ambient form is exactly B.

Unfolding ofSubmodule gives S as its carrier field, so the equality is definitional. The retained IsLattice assumption supplies the full finitely generated submodule required by [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L196) passes.
The other constructor data field also remains the supplied form.

This extends a chosen integral carrier basis to the same vectors in V. Clearing rational denominators preserves linear independence, while fullness gives spanning, as in [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67). The basis is explicitly chosen, not canonical independently of that choice. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L115) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L124) passes.
The extended basis vectors equal the embedded chosen integer basis vectors.
Both bases have the same finite rank.

The equality identifies each extended basis vector with the ambient image of the chosen carrier basis vector. This is the evaluation equation of [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67), so extending scalars changes the coefficient field without changing the vectors. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L124) passes.
The two bases retain the same rank.

The integral basis and its rational extension have the same index set; taking finite ranks gives rankℤ L=dimℚ V. This is the lattice rank comparison in [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67). Degenerate forms do not affect this module-theoretic equality. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L115) passes.
The basis extension retains the same indexed vectors.

The finite set of basis vectors generates its ℤ-span, and taking the ℚ-span of that span recovers all of V. These are exactly the two obligations in [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67). Finite ι suffices; an empty basis correctly yields the zero-dimensional case. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L239) passes.
The lattice constructor uses precisely this integral span as its carrier.

The carrier is spanℤ(b), and bilinearity propagates the assumed integral B(bi,bj) values to all finite integer combinations. Fullness follows from b being a rational basis. This realizes the finite free symmetric pairing described by [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L239) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L244) passes.
The constructor carrier is the actual integer span.
The constructor retains the original ambient pairing.

Restricting b to its ℤ-span gives the carrier basis of the Gram lattice. Independence over ℤ follows from independence over ℚ, and the span gives generation, matching the basis description in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The basis depends on b, while G determines its pairing. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L96) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L301) passes.
The integral hyperbolic basis embeds as the standard coordinate basis.
Its Gram entries are the supplied integers Gij.

The carrier field is definitionally spanℤ(b); G changes the form but not the carrier. This is the construction of a lattice from a basis and Gram matrix in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). No matrix-invertibility premise is needed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L146) passes.
Even for the singular affine Gram matrix the carrier is exactly the integer coordinate vectors.

The form field of ofSubmodule is definitionally B, so its evaluation on all ambient vectors is unchanged. The supplied submodule controls which values must be integral, according to [Mathlib’s integral dual pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L191) passes.
The simultaneously retained carrier is exactly the supplied submodule.

Casting the integer pairing to ℚ, replacing the embedded basis vectors by bi,bj, and applying [Mathlib’s matrix–bilinear-form equivalence](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L191) yields the cast of Gij. Injectivity of ℤ→ℚ recovers exactly Gij, confirming the stated integral Gram entries. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L103) passes.
The concrete hyperbolic Gram matrix is recovered in the integral carrier basis.

The form field is definitionally Matrix.toBilin b applied to the entrywise cast of G. By [Mathlib’s matrix–bilinear-form equivalence](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L191), its value is ∑ij xi Gij yj in b-coordinates; the equality therefore fixes the full rational pairing, including its normalization. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L186) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L165) passes.
The singular affine matrix evaluates as 2(x0−x1)(y0−y1).
The negative rank-one Gram entry gives −2xy.

The equality unfolds the carrier field of ofBasis as the ℤ-span of b. This retains the integral, rather than rational, span of the basis, as required by [Mathlib’s lattice definition and basis extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean#L67). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L279) passes.
The specialized Gram constructor preserves this same integral span.

The form field of ofBasis is definitionally the supplied B. Integer-valuedness on basis pairs proves its integrality on the carrier but does not modify its rational values, consistently with [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L284) passes.
The Gram specialization retains precisely its matrix-defined rational pairing.

The basis of the carrier is b restricted to its integer span, so coercing its ith vector back to V gives bi. This is the embedded-basis convention of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); the equality has no dependence on a choice of matrix inverse. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L96) passes.
For the hyperbolic lattice the equation gives the ordinary coordinate vectors.

Flipping the bilinear form exchanges its two arguments, and the stored symmetry identifies B(y,x) with B(x,y). Extensionality gives equality of forms, precisely the symmetry convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), including for degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L175) passes.
The same symmetry persists on the integer-valued carrier restriction.

For f:H→K, g∘f is the identity point exactly when g kills the ideal generated by f(ker ε_H), matching [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). Published [surjective-coordinate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L94) and [augmentation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L212) controls pass. The ideal lies in K and describes the group kernel, not the ordinary algebra kernel of f in H.
Surjective coordinate morphisms have augmentation as their scheme-kernel ideal.
Augmentation ideal cuts out exactly the identity point.

The cut-out subgroup in K(A) consists exactly of points sent to the convolution identity in H(A), the kernel formula of [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). The published [pointwise criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Kernel.lean#L43) passes. Equality is of subgroups for every A; neither surjectivity of f nor flatness is required for extension of its source augmentation ideal.
Point lies in the cut-out group kernel exactly when its composite is the convolution identity.

Both paths send a quotient point f to χ∘f∘q, by associativity and the quotient map of [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). The published [cross-universe naturality control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Naturality.lean#L50) passes. The statement varies the value algebra covariantly while fixing H and I; it does not perform base change of the coordinate Hopf algebra.
Quotient-point inclusion commutes with postcomposition across value-algebra universes.

Postcomposing by χ and precomposing by q commute because both composites are χ∘f∘q, consistent with [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). The published [bundled naturality control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Naturality.lean#L41) passes. Separate universes for A and B are explicit; no restriction on their cardinalities or extra Hopf structure is introduced.
Quotient-point inclusion is natural in the value algebra.

If g kills I, then χ∘g kills I since χ(0)=0, so the factorization criterion of [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482) remains true. The published [bundled preservation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Naturality.lean#L77) passes. This is preservation of membership, not reflection: an arbitrary χ may kill additional values.
Bundled postcomposition preserves subgroup membership.

A value-algebra morphism preserves the equations g(I)=0, hence sends the cut-out subgroup into its counterpart over B, by [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). This bundles continuous maps in both directions and existence of homotopies from both composites to their respective identities. It is the ordinary, unbased homotopy-equivalence notion; the inverse equations are not strict and the homotopies are not extra chosen data. The structure adds commutative multiplication to NormedRing while retaining the same norm and metric. It is the usual commutative normed-ring notion with submultiplicativity, without completeness or norm-one normalization. In particular it does not assert that the norm is a valuation. Compared with [the reference](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Introduction_to_Berkovich_Spaces.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L134).

The structure retains additive seminorm geometry and submultiplicative associative multiplication while omitting a multiplicative identity. This is the expected nonunital seminormed-ring generalization; the essential product estimate makes no use of a unit. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L39).

This mixin records exactly norm(1)=1, independently of the ring and metric structures. It supplies the normalization that general normed rings lack. With a seminormed additive group it forces nontriviality; with only a raw Norm and One, that further conclusion would not follow. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L165).

The class encodes a group with a left-invariant pseudometric via d(x,y)=norm(-x+y). Additive notation does not assume commutativity. This matches the group-seminorm construction, allowing distinct points at distance zero without promising invariance under right translations. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L186).

A normed additive commutative group is an abelian group whose metric is induced by its norm. Metric separation gives norm(x)=0 only at zero. This is an additive norm notion, with no scalar field or scalar homogeneity assumed. Compared with [the reference](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Introduction_to_Berkovich_Spaces.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L250).

An additive group seminorm on an abelian group constructs the corresponding seminormed-group structure, using d(x,y)=f(-x+y) and norm=f. Symmetry and the triangle inequality come from the seminorm laws. A zero seminorm correctly produces the zero pseudometric. Compared with [the reference](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Introduction_to_Berkovich_Spaces.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L429).

Left multiplication on a nonunital seminormed ring satisfies both IsBoundedSMul estimates with constant one. The vector-variable estimate uses x(y₁−y₂), and the scalar-variable estimate uses (x₁−x₂)y. Distributivity and submultiplicativity suffice without a unit or commutative multiplication. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/MulAction.lean#L60).

A nonunital seminormed ring has continuous addition, negation and jointly continuous multiplication in its seminorm topology. The product proof bounds xy−ab by norm(x)·norm(y−b)+norm(x−a)·norm(b). This local estimate needs neither separation nor completeness. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Lemmas.lean#L179).

The bundle is a bijective semilinear map with inverse scalar homomorphism. For the identity scalar homomorphism it is precisely a linear isomorphism. The inverse-pair assumptions make the inverse semilinear in the opposite direction; no topology, basis or finite-dimensionality is needed. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Defs.lean#L49).

Composition sends x to e₂₃(e₁₂(x)), with scalar homomorphism σ₂₃∘σ₁₂ and inverse e₁₂⁻¹∘e₂₃⁻¹. The scalar-composition and inverse-pair hypotheses certify the displayed semilinear result. The order agrees with ordinary composition of linear isomorphisms. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Defs.lean#L308).

A LinearMap over σ preserves addition and transports scalar multiplication through σ. Ordinary linear maps use the identity homomorphism. Even over semirings, zero preservation follows from the scalar-zero law, so the AddHom parent does not accidentally admit a nonzero constant term. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L84).

This is the standard unital left-module structure, extended from rings to semirings and additive commutative monoids. Both distributive laws, action associativity and the identity action are present; scalar zero acts as zero explicitly. Thus the name also covers what is often called a semimodule. Compared with [the reference](https://faculty.niu.edu/math_beachy/aaol/modules.shtml) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Defs.lean#L54).

The algebra structure is a unital homomorphism from the commutative scalar semiring into the center of A, together with the compatible scalar action. A may be noncommutative. The homomorphism is not required to be injective: quotient algebras remain valid despite the field docstring calling it an embedding. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/algebra-ch05.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Defs.lean#L95).

ContinuousSMul requires joint continuity of the map (c,x)↦c•x in the product topology. It captures the scalar-multiplication part of a topological vector space, generalized to an arbitrary scalar operation. It does not by itself supply any module laws or Hausdorff assumption. Compared with [the reference](https://apps.math.msu.edu/PageSpace/pb/jeffrey-schenker/Teaching/920Notes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/MulAction.lean#L43).

ContinuousConstSMul requires continuity of x↦c•x for every fixed scalar c. The scalar type needs no topology, which is exactly right for this one-variable condition. Joint scalar continuity and norm estimates are deliberately stronger, separate properties. Compared with [the reference](https://apps.math.msu.edu/PageSpace/pb/jeffrey-schenker/Teaching/920Notes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/ConstMulAction.lean#L61).

Addition and subtraction in a seminormed abelian group are uniformly continuous for its existing pseudometric uniformity. The proof bounds the difference map on a product by the sum of its two coordinate distances, giving Lipschitz constant 2 for the maximum product metric. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Uniform.lean#L383).

At coordinate a, a finite sum of coordinate-single functions returns f(a) when a belongs to the finite index set and zero otherwise. Only the matching index can contribute. The statement works for dependent coefficient groups and needs no scalar structure or finite ambient index type. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Piecewise.lean#L174).

An additive monoid homomorphism commutes with every finite sum. Preservation of zero handles the empty sum and preservation of addition handles insertion. The bundled homomorphism-class assumptions are essential; an arbitrary function is not being moved through the sum. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Defs.lean#L365).
